summary.short: Regulation (EU) 2025/327 creates the European Health Data Space: rights of natural persons to access, correct and port their electronic health data, duties for Member States, healthcare providers and health data holders, designated digital health authorities, and a cross-border infrastructure for primary and secondary use of health data.
summary.long: Regulation (EU) 2025/327 establishes the European Health Data Space (EHDS), with common rules, standards, infrastructures and governance for primary use of electronic health data (healthcare provision) and, as Article 1 states, for secondary use. For primary use it gives natural persons rights to access their priority-category data free of charge through electronic health data access services, to insert information, to request rectification, to transmit data to providers of their choice and to restrict access. Member States may delay access for patient-safety reasons and may provide an opt-out from access. Healthcare providers must register priority-category data in an electronic format and may not charge data subjects fees for sharing or accessing data. Member States must designate digital health authorities and a national contact point for digital health, and must connect providers and pharmacies to the MyHealth@EU infrastructure, in which the Commission acts as processor. The Commission is empowered to adopt technical specifications, including the European electronic health record exchange format. Supervisory authorities may impose administrative fines up to the amount referred to in GDPR Article 83(5). Recital 115 states that the Regulation applies from 26 March 2027. The annotated text is the first part (Articles 1 to 23) of the regulation.

notes: Part 1 of 2. Covers the Recitals (1) to (115), which are context only and were not coded as obligations or thresholds, and Articles 1 to 23 (Chapter I; Chapter II Sections 1 to 3). Articles 24 onward, the entry-into-force and application provisions, and the Annexes are in part 2. The application date of 26 March 2027 appears in recital (115) and in the implementation deadlines of Arts 13(4), 15(1), 19(1), 23(2) and 23(4). Several relations are stated only in the title, recitals or Art 1(3)/(5) and are coded as stated. Arts 2(1)(b), (e), (g), (h) and 2(2)(p) also import definitions from other acts (Directive 2011/24/EU, Regulation 2014/24/EU, Regulations 1338/2008 and 765/2008); these are not coded as separate rows. Art 1(3) also lists Regulations 223/2009 and 536/2014, which are not coded individually. Art 3(1) provides immediate access while Art 3(3) allows Member States to delay access. Recital (23) states Denmark's legal system does not allow administrative fines, and that its fines are imposed by courts as criminal penalties. No registry instrument IDs were supplied, so target_instrument_id is empty throughout. No LEIs or tickers apply to the public bodies listed. Part 2 of 2 (Art. 24 to the Annexes). Relations and entities are drawn only from this part. External acts have target_instrument_id left empty because no registry IDs were verified. Art. 43(3) refers to digital health authorities designated under Art. 19, which lies in part 1 and is not annotated here. Art. 105 applies different provisions on different dates (2027, 2029, 2031, 2035); Art. 75(5) applies from 26 March 2035 although the rest of Chapter IV applies from 26 March 2029.
